rules.name: Methodology Requirement
rules.desc:
Methodology courses should be selected based on their potential to support the student’s projected capstone project.
Methodology courses must be taken for 3-5 units and a letter grade.
rules.notes: Note that Methodology courses may not be offered every year. For an up-to-date list of this academic year’s Methodology courses, visit the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website.

rules.name: Community-Engaged Learning Requirement
rules.desc: CCSRE students must complete at least one Community-Engaged Learning (CEL) course or co-curricular experience that centers issues of race, ethnicity, and inequality. This requirement may be fulfilled by enrolling in a Cardinal Course, completing a CCSRE Undergraduate Fellowship, or participating in an Alternative Spring Break. The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by courses that also fulfill other Native American Studies degree requirements (e.g., a Methodology course may also count toward the CEL requirement). The CEL requirement may be fulfilled by academic experiences, such as fellowships, that do not carry academic units.
rules.notes: See the Community-Engaged Learning course list on the Core Coursework page on the CCSRE website for this year’s curricular offerings.

rules.name: Native American Studies Electives

limits.label: DAAAS, ASNAMST, CHILATST, CSRE or JEWISHST courses

rules.desc:
Native American Studies majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in Native American Studies. Exceptions are listed below.

• Native American Studies majors may count up to 8 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity (CSRE), or Jewish Studies (JEWISHST) courses toward their degree in Native American Studies.

• Native American Studies majors may count up to 5 units of a Native language listed in Special Languages (see below) toward the major degree.

rules.name: Language Study (optional)
rules.desc: Students may apply up to 5 units of Native language coursework listed in Special Languages toward their Native American Studies degree.

rules.name: At most two S/NC classes, and only as electives
Writing in the Major (WIM)
rules.notes:
CCSRE students must plan to complete 200X or 201X in person on Stanford campus in autumn of their final year of study.
Note that the same five-unit course fulfills the WIM and Capstone requirements.

rules.name: Honors (optional)
rules.desc:
Honors students must apply with a complete proposal approved by a CCSRE faculty advisor in the spring preceding their final year of study. Honors students must continuously enroll at Stanford in autumn, winter, and spring. For more information about the Honors program and the application process, visit the Honors page on the CCSRE website.
Honors applications are open to students with a grade point average (GPA) of at least 3.7 in the major and 3.5 overall. Students must receive a grade of B+ or above on their thesis and maintain the GPA minimum until graduation in order to receive Honors.
rules.notes: A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the WIM and Capstone requirements.

grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade, unless only offered S/NC. A minimum grade of C- is required for a student to count a class towards the Core Curriculum, including the Gateway, Comparative Core, Major Core, Methodology, WIM, and Capstone requirements. Additional units toward the major require a passing grade of D- or above. Student may count 2 classes with Satisfactory/No Credit (SNC) grading basis toward Additional Units.
policies: No more than 15 units of petitioned courses that are not listed under CCSRE or cross-listed with CCSRE may be applied to electives in the Native American Studies major. Students who wish to petition a course must fill out and submit a course petition form for the CCSRE Academic Programs team to review within one month of completing their annual degree audit meeting with the CCSRE Student Services Officer.
transferPolicy: Up to 20 units of external credit may be applied toward elective coursework in the major.
reviewNotes: The audit checks CSRE 100, two of CSRE 101A, 101B and 101C, NATIVEAM 100, a methodology course (3-5 units), a Community-Engaged Learning course (which may also count elsewhere), WIM and the capstone (CSRE 200X or 201X), and electives to reach 60 units: Native American Studies courses, with at most 8 units from other CCSRE programs, 5 units of Native language and 15 units of petitioned courses outside CCSRE. Required courses must be letter graded (unless offered only S/NC), and the core, methodology, WIM and capstone courses need a C- or better. Checked by hand: that no more than two classes are S/NC, and only as electives, and that at most 20 units are external credit. Honors is optional.
